newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CLB SAYS 850 MLN BFR STOLEN, INSURANCE TO COVER.
newsitem.headline: CLB SAYS 850 MLN BFR STOLEN, INSURANCE TO COVER.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais Belgium (CLB), a unit of French Credit Lyonnais, on Thursday confirmed reports in Belgian media that an employee stole 850 million Belgian francs from the Belgian bank.
CLB chief executive officer Philippe Cloes said that the bank hoped to recover part of the money and that whatever amount that was not recovered would be covered by the insurance.
There would be no impact on 1996 earnings, he said. In 1995 CLB earned a 628 million franc profit.
The employee was a woman in CLB's Ghent office. Her husband, who is chairman of a Belgian soccer team, is also under arrest, he said.

"She has confessed to the police that she has stolen 850 million. Several millions have already been blocked on accounts in Belgium and abroad. We expect to recuperate several millions that way," Cloes said.
"Even if there is no recuperation, there will be no impact on earnings. Our insurance covers for 100 percent any thefts by employees," he added.

Asked how an employee could steal such a large amount -- bigger than the bank's 1995 earnings -- Cloes said: "Billions of francs move around every day in our bank. If one steals 20 million once a month, you don't see it."

"The lady had been with us for 30 years, we had absolute confidence in her." He said she probably started diverting funds in a limited way in 1992, but that in recent months the amounts had become bigger.
For CLB, which in 1995 suffered from negative press coverage of financial problems at its French parent company, the theft is another blow to its image.
"For our image it is a catastrophe," Cloes said.
He said CLB will publish 1996 earnings at the end of the month. No precise date has been fixed yet. The bank earned 628 million francs in 1995 and 1,272 million in 1994.

CLB is a relatively small player in the Belgian banking world. At the end of June 30, 1996 it had total assets of 547 billion francs, about a 10th of those of market leader Generale Bank . But its aggressive marketing policy and sharp pricing make it one of the most high-profile players in the industry.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
